drafted_from: tools/research-a-creator-or-topic/tool-rows.json (tool:list-the-items-in-a-saved-file), do-work/research-from-this-computer.mjs (savedList) and sources.mjs, test/commands.test.mjs; the example was run here on synthetic files
start_here: Say to your AI: "Read my saved list in bookmarks.json into items I can research, and tell me what it holds." It runs the saved-list command on your computer and reads the items from the file it writes.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads one JSON file you saved on your computer and writes its items to another JSON file.
instructions: 1. Clone the Workshop repository; the only thing needed is node. Nothing leaves your computer.
2. Point at the file: a JSON array of rows, or an object holding rows under sources, bookmarks, items, records, rows or data, or a browser sidebar file (--shape browser-sidebar).

3. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:list-the-items-in-a-saved-file"} and runs: node trillion-workshop/tools/research-a-creator-or-topic/do-work/research-from-this-computer.mjs saved-list --file bookmarks.json --out items.json (add --limit N to cut the list; 5000 is the most).

4. Read the last line, {"result": {source, subject_ref, count, out}}, then items.json: each row has item_id, title, url, published, description, source_family, source_type, container_path, license_status (unknown when the row says nothing) and lifecycle_status. A failure prints {"failed": {code, message}} with exit 2: bad-request or unreadable-file.
